PullRequest.Title: Don't listen on menu changed, method 2
PullRequest.Body:
This time, instead of only updating the tree elements who's actions are visible (selected, focused, focusing), update all tree items that the context change applies to, as before. However, the context key change event is now per tree renderer, not per menu.
Fixes #213145

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Virtual dispatch makes the superclass refresh use the subclass sorting implementation, and the first pass does not depend on subclass fields. The second call is therefore demonstrably duplicate work; only absolute menu size varies.
Findings.PerformanceResource: menu-item array copies, O(M log M) sorting, group arrays, and context-expression traversal
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Every MenuInfo construction now performs two complete passes over M entries; recursive submenus repeat the duplicate pass, and large menus such as CommandPalette include the full command registry.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased startup and interaction latency with extra allocation and GC pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before the refactor, the MenuInfo constructor called refresh exactly once, producing one copied, sorted, and grouped menu snapshot per construction.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: MenuInfoSnapshot's constructor now calls this.refresh(), which dynamically dispatches _sort to MenuInfo's override and fully builds the sorted groups. The added this.refresh() in the subclass constructor immediately repeats the same MenuRegistry copy, sort, grouping, and context-key collection.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT-side this.refresh() at menuService.ts:265 is a second immediate invocation after the newly added superclass constructor already invoked refresh.
Findings.Title: Initialize each MenuInfo only once
Findings.Impact: Opening the command palette, constructing startup toolbars and menus, and rendering custom-tree rows all synchronously pay twice for menu snapshot initialization. The command-palette path is especially large because it includes all registered commands.
Findings.Evidence: MenuInfoSnapshot's constructor calls refresh at menuService.ts:177. refresh calls the virtual _sort, so the first call already uses MenuInfo._sort and fully initializes the snapshot. The subclass calls refresh again at line 265. MenuRegistry.getMenuItems allocates an array and appends all commands for CommandPalette; CommandsQuickAccessProvider creates that menu on its opening critical path. createActionGroups also recursively constructs MenuInfo for submenus.
Findings.Recommendation: Invoke refresh only once: remove the subclass call if the base constructor remains eager, or make the base constructor non-eager and call refresh once after subclass initialization.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous call path and allocation sites are explicit, and the before/after cache behavior is visible in the deleted per-row MenuImpl listener versus the added snapshot call. Exact row/menu counts vary by viewport and installed extensions, which affects magnitude but not the O(R*M) mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: MenuRegistry item-array copies, context-expression traversals, and transient Map/Set objects on the UI thread
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For every global context-key event, cost grows as O(R * M), where R is the number of rendered custom-tree rows after virtualization and M is the total number of built-in and extension-contributed ViewItemContext menu entries; this occurs even when the changed key is unrelated to the menu.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased UI-thread CPU and GC pressure, causing interaction latency or dropped frames while custom trees are visible
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Each rendered row retained a MenuImpl whose MenuInfo collected the menu's dependency sets once when that row was rendered. Subsequent context events checked the cached sets with affectsSome; they did not rescan MenuRegistry or allocate a new dependency snapshot per row and event.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The renderer now handles every context event itself and, inside the nested rendered-row loop, calls getEntireMenuContexts(). That method constructs MenuInfoSnapshot, copies and traverses all ViewItemContext entries, and allocates another Set on every invocation.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT-side condition at treeView.ts:1441 places getEntireMenuContexts() inside both loops over _renderedElements; getEntireMenuContexts and the uncached MenuService.getMenuContexts implementation are also added by this diff.
Findings.Title: Hoist menu-context discovery out of the row loop
Findings.Impact: With a custom tree showing tens of rows and extensions contributing many view-item actions, ordinary global context updates such as focus/editor/context changes synchronously repeat the full menu scan once per row, including for keys that ultimately do not rerender anything.
Findings.Evidence: TreeRenderer is instantiated with the workbench context service and subscribes directly to onDidChangeContext at line 1208. At line 1441 each rendered element calls TreeMenus.getEntireMenuContexts; that delegates to MenuService.getMenuContexts, which creates a new MenuInfoSnapshot and Set. MenuInfoSnapshot.refresh calls MenuRegistry.getMenuItems (itself an array copy) and traverses every item's when/precondition/toggled expressions. The prior MenuImpl listener at menuService.ts:417-425 uses its already-populated MenuInfo sets instead.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep one dependency snapshot per renderer/menu ID and refresh it on ViewItemContext registry changes, or at minimum compute it once before entering the rendered-row loops. Reuse fixed overlay-key sets rather than allocating a Map per row/event.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The old 50 ms DebounceEmitter and the new immediate call path to per-row DOM rebuilding are explicit. Frequency of relevant extension-defined context updates varies, so severity is medium, but any burst deterministically multiplies work.
Findings.PerformanceResource: synchronous tree list splices, action-object construction/disposal, and DOM action-bar nodes
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For U rapid updates to a context key used by ViewItemContext actions, work grows as O(U * R * A), where R is affected rendered rows and A is the per-row action/render work; the previous 50 ms menu debounce collapsed updates within the window.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: blocked UI-thread time and dropped frames during bursts of relevant context-key updates
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Each row listened to MenuImpl.onDidChange. MenuImpl uses a DebounceEmitter with the default 50 ms delay, so repeated relevant context changes were merged before the row was rerendered.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added direct ContextKeyService listener invokes onDidChangeContext synchronously for every event. An affected event immediately fires all matching items, and the added listener at line 721 calls tree.rerender separately for each; rerender reaches list.splice and renderElement, which clears/recreates action-bar DOM and rebuilds menu actions.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT-side subscription at treeView.ts:1208 replaces the deleted MenuImpl.onDidChange subscriptions but adds no scheduler, debounce, or event/item coalescing before synchronous rerendering.
Findings.Title: Restore coalescing before rerendering tree rows
Findings.Impact: An extension or workbench feature that updates a view-item menu context several times during one operation now forces a complete visible-row action rebuild for every intermediate update instead of one coalesced rebuild, making tree interactions visibly janky.
Findings.Evidence: MenuService.createMenu defaults eventDebounceDelay to 50 ms, and MenuImpl.onDidChange is a DebounceEmitter using that delay at menuService.ts:426-435. The deleted TreeMenus code subscribed to that debounced event. The new subscription at treeView.ts:1208 is directly on ContextKeyService; treeView.ts:1447 fires synchronously, treeView.ts:721 rerenders every item, asyncDataTree.ts:578-585 reaches the tree rerender, and ActionBar.clear/push disposes and creates DOM nodes.
Findings.Recommendation: Use one renderer-level debounce/run-once scheduler (preserving the prior delay or scheduling once per frame), merge changed keys and deduplicate affected item handles, then rerender each row once after the burst.

Scenarios.Scenario: A custom extension tree is visible while unrelated global context keys change during editor focus, cursor, configuration, or extension activity.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ContextKeyService synchronously invokes the new TreeRenderer listener. Before the event can return, the renderer visits every rendered row and reconstructs the complete ViewItemContext dependency set; unrelated keys stop after these checks, so row rendering is off this scenario's path but repeated registry work is not.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: R rendered rows after tree virtualization (typically viewport-sized, but potentially tens to around a hundred) multiplied by M built-in and installed-extension contributions to view/item/context, for every global context event.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All work is serialized on the UI thread. There is one renderer listener rather than one listener per row, but its nested loop has no scheduling, limiter, or coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Previously each row's retained MenuInfo cached structure/precondition/toggled dependency sets after rendering. The changed getMenuContexts path has no cold/warm distinction: each row and event copies MenuRegistry entries, traverses expressions, and allocates new sets/maps.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the direct event subscription, nested row loops, uncached snapshot constructor, MenuRegistry array copy, and expression traversal are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installed extension menu counts and context-event frequency vary, but every event while a custom tree is present follows the O(R*M) path even when unrelated.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression because the diff replaces cached dependency checks with uncached per-row registry reconstruction on a frequent synchronous UI event path. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network calls are reached.

Scenarios.Scenario: A context key used by custom-tree inline or context actions changes repeatedly while the tree is visible.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each relevant ContextKeyService event immediately computes affected rows, fires onDidChangeMenuContext, and calls tree.rerender once per row. Each rerender performs a list splice and renderElement clears/recreates action-bar actions and DOM before the event completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Tree list splice followed by ActionBar disposal and creation of action DOM nodes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One boundary crossing per affected rendered row per context event; bursts multiply this by the number of updates because there is no coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same eventual row rendering existed, but MenuImpl.onDidChange's 50 ms DebounceEmitter collapsed bursts before the tree listener ran.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously before the context event returns and can block input/rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: U relevant context updates multiplied by R affected rendered rows and A actions/DOM nodes rebuilt per row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous, sequential UI-thread rerenders with no renderer-level debounce or item deduplication across events. Previously each row's MenuImpl merged changes for 50 ms before notifying its listener.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Menu actions are reconstructed through a fresh, immediately disposed MenuImpl on every rerender. There is no coalesced warm path; repeated values within the prior debounce window still rebuild.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the deleted listener was behind MenuImpl's explicit 50 ms DebounceEmitter, while the new listener invokes rerender synchronously.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The prevalence of extensions or workbench features that burst-update a menu dependency varies, but any such burst deterministically changes from roughly one rebuild window to U rebuilds.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable missing-coalescing regression with synchronous rendering and allocation pressure. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network calls are reached.

Scenarios.Scenario: Menus are constructed during startup, custom-tree row rendering/scrolling, context-menu opening, or command-palette opening.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: MenuService.createMenu/getMenuActions constructs MenuImpl, which constructs MenuInfo before actions are available. MenuInfoSnapshot's superclass constructor fully refreshes the snapshot, then the subclass constructor immediately refreshes it again; both passes must finish before the menu or row can render.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: M entries in the requested menu, plus recursively reached submenu entries. CommandPalette is high-cardinality because getMenuItems appends the full command registry; custom-tree rendering repeats construction for each row rendered.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Both full passes are serialized synchronously on the UI thread. Recursive submenu construction repeats the duplicate passes; no limiter or deferred phase applies.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: MenuRegistry data is resident in memory, but getMenuItems creates a new array and sorting/grouping/context-key collection are redone on every refresh. Warm menu construction still pays both passes; there is no snapshot reuse.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: superclass construction calls refresh, refresh dynamically dispatches the subclass sort, and the added subclass line calls refresh again without intervening state changes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Absolute menu sizes and construction counts vary by startup configuration and extensions, but the second pass is exactly duplicate for every MenuInfo.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression because all menu construction now doubles snapshot copy/sort/traversal, including the high-cardinality command palette. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network calls are reached.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and all diff pages. Submitted three findings: uncached per-row menu dependency reconstruction on every context event, removal of the prior 50 ms coalescing before synchronous tree rerenders, and duplicate MenuInfo initialization across all menu construction. Checked custom-tree event/render/context-menu paths and general/command-palette menu construction; no transitive subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundaries were introduced.
